translationRepairs: In 756, the first year of Zhide, a Huainan circuit military commissioner was created, commanding thirteen prefectures—Yang, Chu, Chu, He, Shou, Lu, Shu, Guang, Qi, An, Huang, Shen, and Mian—from his seat at Yang Prefecture.

In 756, the first year of Zhide, a Huainan circuit military commissioner was created, commanding thirteen prefectures—Yang, Chǔ, Chú, He, Shou, Lu, Shu, Guang, Qi, An, Huang, Shen, and Mian—from his seat at Yang Prefecture.
The source list contains both 楚 (Chǔ) and 滁 (Chú). Tone-marked pinyin preserves the distinction without putting Chinese characters in the English field.

756, first year of the Zhide era. The Huainan circuit military commissioner was established, holding Yang, Chu, Chu, He, Shou, Lu, Shu, Guang, Qi, An, Huang, Shen, and Mian prefectures—thirteen in all—with seat at Yang Prefecture.

756, first year of the Zhide era. The Huainan circuit military commissioner was established, holding Yang, Chǔ, Chú, He, Shou, Lu, Shu, Guang, Qi, An, Huang, Shen, and Mian prefectures—thirteen in all—with seat at Yang Prefecture.
The literal field likewise collapses the distinct prefectures 楚 (Chǔ) and 滁 (Chú); tone-marked pinyin disambiguates them cleanly.

In 757, the second year of Zhide, a Jiannan East Chuan military commissioner was appointed, commanding twelve prefectures—Zi, Sui, Mian, Jian, Long, Lang, Pu, Ling, Lu, Rong, Zi, and Jian—from his seat at Zi Prefecture.

In 757, the second year of Zhide, a Jiannan East Chuan military commissioner was appointed, commanding twelve prefectures—Zǐ, Sui, Mian, Jiàn, Long, Lang, Pu, Ling, Lu, Rong, Zī, and Jiǎn—from his seat at Zi Prefecture.
The source enumerates the distinct prefectures 梓 (Zǐ) and 資 (Zī) as well as 劍 (Jiàn) and 簡 (Jiǎn). Tone marks distinguish both pairs without Chinese characters in the English field.

757, second year. The Jiannan East Chuan circuit military commissioner was established, holding Zi, Sui, Mian, Jian, Long, Lang, Pu, Ling, Lu, Rong, Zi, and Jian prefectures—twelve in all—with seat at Zi Prefecture.

757, second year. The Jiannan East Chuan circuit military commissioner was established, holding Zǐ, Sui, Mian, Jiàn, Long, Lang, Pu, Ling, Lu, Rong, Zī, and Jiǎn prefectures—twelve in all—with seat at Zi Prefecture.
The literal list also loses the distinctions between 梓/資 and 劍/簡; tone-marked pinyin accurately differentiates the prefectures.
The Wuchang Army circuit was restored.
In 850, the fourth year, the Wuchang Army circuit was restored.
The unit begins 850 四年, so the idiomatic translation must retain the year and year number before the restoration of the Wuchang Army circuit.
The Wuchang Army circuit was again established.
850, fourth year. The Wuchang Army circuit was again established.
The literal translation also omits the explicit date 850 四年; the proposed wording restores it faithfully.
